    /* ---------- Icon normalization ----------
       Phosphor 1.4.2 uses font-icons via :before content, which inherit the
       body line-height (1.5) and render off-center inside flex/grid hosts.
       Forcing line-height:1 + inline-flex display gives every icon a square
       intrinsic box that centers cleanly. The same applies to our custom
       inline .x-icon SVG so the X mark sits on the same baseline grid as the
       Phosphor glyphs.
       text-decoration:none ensures icons inside <a> never inherit underline
       from a hover state on the link. */

    [class*=" ph-"],
    .x-icon {
      display: inline-flex;
      align-items: center;
      justify-content: center;
      line-height: 1;
      vertical-align: middle;
      flex: 0 0 auto;
      text-decoration: none;

    <section id="failover">
      <div class="wrap">
        <div class="section-head">
          <span class="eyebrow"><i class="ph-warning-circle" aria-hidden="true"></i>The tracer, honestly</span>
          <h2>What the tracer assumes, and how it stays honest.</h2>
          <p>Glasshouse is transparent observability over your own swarm, and that has boundaries. They are documented,
            and where reality bends them, there is an explicit choice rather than a silent fudge.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="table-wrap">
          <table class="behavior">
            <thead>
              <tr>
                <th>Assumption or property</th>
                <th>What it means</th>
                <th>How Glasshouse handles it</th>
              </tr>
            </thead>
            <tbody>
              <tr>
                <td data-label="Assumption">You instrument the swarm</td>
                <td data-label="Means">Glasshouse sees only the steps you wrap in observe(); it does not auto-discover untraced calls.</td>
                <td data-label="Handling">Wrap each agent step and tag a span kind; an unwrapped call simply does not appear in the graph, by design.</td>
              </tr>
              <tr>
                <td data-label="Assumption">Observability, not control</td>
                <td data-label="Means">Glasshouse watches the swarm; it does not route, retry, or call any model itself.</td>
                <td data-label="Handling">It records spans, builds the graph, and detects drift; control belongs to your orchestrator, not to the tracer.</td>
              </tr>
              <tr>
                <td data-label="Assumption">Nine span kinds</td>
                <td data-label="Means">A span is one of agent, reasoning, llm, tool, memory, state, decision, verification, or handoff.</td>
                <td data-label="Handling">The fixed taxonomy keeps the graph typed and renderable; arbitrary custom kinds are a documented non-goal for 1.0.</td>
              </tr>
              <tr>
                <td data-label="Assumption">Cost is read from the span</td>
                <td data-label="Means">Per-step cost comes from the token counts your client reports on the llm span.</td>
                <td data-label="Handling">When no counts are reported a step shows zero cost; the tally never invents a number it cannot read.</td>
              </tr>
              <tr>
                <td data-label="Assumption">Statistical drift detection</td>
                <td data-label="Means">Drift is flagged by z-score, EWMA, Page-Hinkley, or PSI over the span stream.</td>
                <td data-label="Handling">A detector reports a signal, not a verdict; you set the threshold and decide what a flag means for your run.</td>
              </tr>
              <tr>
                <td data-label="Assumption">Attribution from the graph</td>
                <td data-label="Means">The culprit agent is inferred from the failed run's graph, not asserted by the agents.</td>
                <td data-label="Handling">It is read off the edges by walking back from the failing node, so attribution is grounded in the trace.</td>
              </tr>
              <tr>
                <td data-label="Assumption">Redaction before export</td>
                <td data-label="Means">Sensitive fields are stripped before a span leaves the process.</td>
                <td data-label="Handling">Redaction runs in the export path, so an exporter never ships a field you marked for redaction.</td>
              </tr>
              <tr>
                <td data-label="Assumption">Integrity, not identity</td>
                <td data-label="Means">The audit seal proves a log was not altered after sealing.</td>
                <td data-label="Handling">A SHA-256 hash chain via Web Crypto, an integrity seal; Ed25519 signs a snapshot for stronger evidence.</td>
              </tr>
            </tbody>
          </table>
        </div>
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="faq" class="alt">
      <div class="wrap">
        <div class="section-head">
          <span class="eyebrow"><i class="ph-question" aria-hidden="true"></i>FAQ</span>
          <h2>Common questions.</h2>
        </div>
        <div class="faq">
          <details open>
            <summary><span>Is Glasshouse production-ready at 1.0.0?</span><i class="ph-plus" aria-hidden="true"></i><i
                class="ph-minus" aria-hidden="true"></i></summary>
            <p>Yes. 115 tests pass across 22 suites under Vitest 4 with coverage about 88.48% of statements; TypeScript
              maximum strict mode is clean; Biome lint is clean; <code>publint</code> and
              <code>@arethetypeswrong/cli</code> are clean across every subpath. The suite and the distribution smoke test
              are run on the Node 20, 22, and 24 matrix. Every published release carries SLSA provenance produced by
              GitHub Actions.
            </p>
          </details>
          <details>
            <summary><span>Why not just read the raw spans yourself?</span><i class="ph-plus" aria-hidden="true"></i><i class="ph-minus"
                aria-hidden="true"></i></summary>
            <p>You can, and a raw OpenTelemetry SDK gives you spans. But a swarm is a graph, not a flat list: you want to
              see which agent handed off to which, where a run looped, and which agent to blame when it failed.
              Glasshouse turns the spans into a renderable agent graph, runs drift and loop detection over the stream, and
              attributes failures, so you read behavior instead of scrolling a span dump.</p>
          </details>
          <details>
            <summary><span>Why not use a closed observability box?</span><i class="ph-plus"
                aria-hidden="true"></i><i class="ph-minus" aria-hidden="true"></i></summary>
            <p>You can, and many do. The cost is a black box that hides which model answered and the path it took, on
              infrastructure you do not own and that may block the EU. Glasshouse is the glass house: it exposes the agent
              graph, the per-step decisions, and the cost, it is OpenTelemetry-native, and it runs in your process on your
              own infrastructure, so the trace is yours to inspect.</p>
          </details>
          <details>
            <summary><span>Does Glasshouse call any model itself?</span><i class="ph-plus"
                aria-hidden="true"></i><i class="ph-minus" aria-hidden="true"></i></summary>
            <p>No. Glasshouse is observability over your own swarm. You wrap each agent step in <code>observe()</code> and
              it records the span, builds the graph, watches for drift, and seals the audit chain. It makes no model calls
              of its own, which keeps it dependency-free and testable with no network, and it means your provider keys
              live in your client, never in Glasshouse.</p>
          </details>
          <details>
            <summary><span>Does this work in Cloudflare Workers, Vercel Edge, Bun, or Deno?</span><i class="ph-plus"
                aria-hidden="true"></i><i class="ph-minus" aria-hidden="true"></i></summary>
            <p>Yes. The core is node-free; it uses the Web Crypto API for SHA-256 and Ed25519, not <code>node:crypto</code>.
              Import <code>@takk/glasshouse</code> or <code>@takk/glasshouse/edge</code> on any runtime with Web Crypto, and
              ship spans with the OTLP or fetch exporter. Only <code>@takk/glasshouse/node</code>, the file exporter and
              JSON loaders, requires the Node standard library.
            </p>
          </details>
          <details>
            <summary><span>How does Glasshouse handle my data?</span><i class="ph-plus" aria-hidden="true"></i><i
                class="ph-minus" aria-hidden="true"></i></summary>
            <p>Glasshouse holds the spans you record, the graph it builds, and the audit chain it seals, nothing else. It
              makes no outbound network calls of its own beyond the exporter you configure, and redaction runs before any
              span leaves the process. With the file loaders, only the trace or run files you point it at are read from
              disk, and no provider credentials are ever held by Glasshouse.</p>
          </details>
          <details>
            <summary><span>What does a span kind actually mean?</span><i
                class="ph-plus" aria-hidden="true"></i><i class="ph-minus" aria-hidden="true"></i></summary>
            <p>A span kind labels what a step did, so the graph is typed and the detectors know what to read. The nine
              kinds are agent, reasoning, llm, tool, memory, state, decision, verification, and handoff. You pass the kind
              to <code>observe()</code>, and Glasshouse uses it to render the node, attribute a failure, and tally cost on
              the llm spans. Read the kinds off the graph to see exactly how the swarm behaved.</p>
          </details>
          <details>
            <summary><span>Is the audit trail a digital signature?</span><i class="ph-plus" aria-hidden="true"></i><i
                class="ph-minus" aria-hidden="true"></i></summary>
            <p>The chain itself is an integrity seal: each entry is chained to the previous one through a SHA-256 hash of
              its canonical form, so any later edit breaks the chain. On top of that, a snapshot can be signed with
              Ed25519 over the Web Crypto API, which does prove who produced it. Use the hash chain for tamper-evidence
              and the signature when you need third-party attribution.</p>
          </details>
          <details>
            <summary><span>Which providers and frameworks does it support?</span><i class="ph-plus"
                aria-hidden="true"></i><i class="ph-minus" aria-hidden="true"></i></summary>
            <p>Any of them. Because you call <code>observe()</code> around your own steps, Glasshouse traces a swarm built
              on OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, a local model, or any framework, treated uniformly as agents in the graph.
              Spans are OpenTelemetry-compatible, so they export to any OTLP backend you already run.</p>
          </details>
          <details>
            <summary><span>Where does the state live?</span><i class="ph-plus" aria-hidden="true"></i><i
                class="ph-minus" aria-hidden="true"></i></summary>
            <p>In-process memory by default, with portable JSON snapshots via <code>snapshot()</code> and
              <code>fromSnapshot()</code>, the spans and the scalar configuration. For disk-backed output, write spans or
              load a saved trace from JSON with <code>@takk/glasshouse/node</code>. For an edge runtime, snapshot to your
              own KV store between invocations, or stream out through the OTLP exporter.
            </p>
          </details>
          <details>
            <summary><span>How does it keep cost visible?</span><i class="ph-plus"
                aria-hidden="true"></i><i class="ph-minus" aria-hidden="true"></i></summary>
            <p>Every llm span carries the token counts your client reports, so the per-step dollar cost is on the node and
              the run-level tally sums it. A runaway agent shows up at once as a costly node in the graph. Glasshouse does
              not cap spend itself, it makes it visible, so your orchestrator can act on the signal, and trace sampling
              keeps the telemetry volume affordable.</p>
          </details>
          <details>
            <summary><span>How do I verify a published version's provenance?</span><i class="ph-plus"

  <script>
    (function () {
      var root = document.documentElement;
      var stored = null;
      try {stored = localStorage.getItem('glasshouse-theme');} catch (_) { }
      if (stored === 'light' || stored === 'dark') {root.setAttribute('data-theme', stored);}
      var btn = document.getElementById('theme-toggle');
      if (btn) {
        btn.addEventListener('click', function () {
          var current = root.getAttribute('data-theme');
          var systemDark = window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches;
          var next;
          if (!current) {next = systemDark ? 'light' : 'dark';}
          else {next = current === 'dark' ? 'light' : 'dark';}
          root.setAttribute('data-theme', next);
          try {localStorage.setItem('glasshouse-theme', next);} catch (_) { }
        });
      }
    }());

    document.querySelectorAll('.copy-btn').forEach(function (btn) {
      btn.addEventListener('click', function () {
        var text = btn.getAttribute('data-copy') || '';
        var label = btn.querySelector('span');
        var orig = label ? label.textContent : 'Copy';
        var done = function () {
          if (label) label.textContent = 'Copied';
          btn.classList.add('copied');
          setTimeout(function () {
            if (label) label.textContent = orig;
            btn.classList.remove('copied');
          }, 1400);
        };
        if (navigator.clipboard && navigator.clipboard.writeText) {
          navigator.clipboard.writeText(text).then(done, done);
        } else {
          try {
            var ta = document.createElement('textarea');
            ta.value = text;
            ta.style.position = 'fixed';
            ta.style.opacity = '0';
            document.body.appendChild(ta);
            ta.select();
            document.execCommand('copy');
            document.body.removeChild(ta);
            done();
          } catch (_) {done();}
        }
      });
    });

    document.querySelectorAll('[role="tablist"]').forEach(function (list) {
      var tabs = list.querySelectorAll('[role="tab"]');
      tabs.forEach(function (tab) {
        tab.addEventListener('click', function () {
          tabs.forEach(function (t) {t.setAttribute('aria-selected', 'false');});
          tab.setAttribute('aria-selected', 'true');
          var targetId = tab.getAttribute('aria-controls');
          var siblings = document.querySelectorAll('.tabpanel[data-active="true"]');
          siblings.forEach(function (panel) {
            if (panel.getAttribute('aria-labelledby') &&
              Array.from(tabs).some(function (t) {return t.id === panel.getAttribute('aria-labelledby');})) {
              panel.setAttribute('data-active', 'false');
            }
          });
          var target = document.getElementById(targetId);
          if (target) target.setAttribute('data-active', 'true');
        });
      });
    });
  </script>
